q: Who is the author and narrator of "A Triumph of Surgery"?
o: James Herriot
Ruskin Bond
Robert Arthur
Victor Canning
e: James Herriot (a veterinary surgeon in real life as well) wrote and narrated "A Triumph of Surgery".

q: Who has written the story "The Thief's Story"?
o: H. G. Wells
K. A. Abbas
James Herriot
Ruskin Bond
e: Celebrated Indian author Ruskin Bond wrote "The Thief's Story", narrated from the young thief's perspective.

q: In "A Triumph of Surgery", who was Tricki?
o: A greyhound
A pet rabbit
A small pampered dog
A Persian cat
e: Tricki was Mrs Pumphrey's small, overfed pet dog who fell ill from excessive luxury and lack of exercise.

q: Who does "I" refer to as the narrator in "The Thief's Story"?
o: Anil
Hari Singh
Ruskin Bond
The publisher
e: The fifteen-year-old thief, who introduces himself as Hari Singh, narrates the story in the first person ("I").

q: Who is Mrs Pumphrey in "A Triumph of Surgery"?
o: A veterinary surgeon
Tricki's wealthy mistress
The gardener's wife
Mr Herriot's assistant
e: Mrs Pumphrey is the rich, over-indulgent owner of Tricki whose excessive pampering causes his illness.

q: What was Hari Singh "a fairly successful hand" at when he met Anil?
o: Stealing
Writing magazine articles
Wrestling
Cooking
e: Right at the opening, the fifteen-year-old narrator confesses, "I was still a thief when I met Anil. And though only 15, I was an experienced and fairly successful hand."

q: What is the main cause of Tricki's ailment in "A Triumph of Surgery"?
o: Cold winter rain
Infection from stray dogs
Food poisoning at the clinic
Overfeeding and lack of exercise
e: Mrs Pumphrey overfed Tricki with rich treats and failed to give him sufficient exercise, making him dangerously obese.

q: What was Anil doing when Hari Singh first approached him?
o: Writing a novel
Waiting for a train
Watching a wrestling match
Buying sweets at Jumna Sweet Shop
e: Hari Singh first met Anil while Anil was watching a wrestling match; Hari flattered him by saying he looked like a wrestler.

q: According to Mrs Pumphrey, what disease was Tricki suffering from?
o: Pneumonia
Hay fever
Malnutrition
Lumbago
e: Seeing Tricki listless and lacking energy, Mrs Pumphrey mistakenly thought he was suffering from malnutrition and fed him even more extras.

q: How often did the young thief change his name?
o: Every week
Every month
Every year
Every day
e: Hari Singh says, "I took a new name every month. That kept me ahead of the police and my former employers."

q: For how many days was Tricki kept without food at Mr Herriot's surgery?
o: Two days
Five days
Fourteen days
One day
e: For two days Mr Herriot kept an eye on Tricki, giving him no food, but plenty of water.

q: What was Anil by profession in "The Thief's Story"?
o: A railway clerk
A lockmaker
A professional wrestler
A writer for magazines
e: Anil was a struggling twenty-five-year-old writer who wrote for magazines and made money by fits and starts.

q: What was the name of Mrs Pumphrey's gardener who was down with lumbago?
o: Joe
Tristan
Henry
Hodgkin
e: Mrs Pumphrey explained that Hodgkin, the gardener, had been down with lumbago, so Tricki had missed his ring-throwing exercise.

q: What name did the young thief give to Anil when introducing himself?
o: Ravi Kumar
Ramlal
Hari Singh
Arun
e: The thief introduced himself to Anil as Hari Singh, adding that it was a false name he had adopted that month.

q: To what did James Herriot compare Tricki's hugely fat appearance on the street?
o: A round football
A bloated sausage with a leg at each corner
A fluffy cloud
A sleeping teddy bear
e: Herriot describes Tricki as "hugely fat, like a bloated sausage with a leg at each corner."

q: Where did Anil live in "The Thief's Story"?
o: In a room over the Jumna Sweet Shop
In a bungalow near the clock tower
Inside the railway station quarters
At Shotover Grange
e: Anil took Hari Singh to his simple room located over the Jumna Sweet Shop.

q: What sweet things could Mrs Pumphrey not bear to refuse Tricki?
o: Cream cakes and chocolates
Ice cream and puddings
Sugar cubes and pastries
Honey biscuits and jalebis
e: Despite Herriot's warning, Mrs Pumphrey confessed she could not bear to refuse Tricki his beloved cream cakes and chocolates.

q: What daily work did Hari Singh do for Anil?
o: Washing Anil's car
Typing manuscripts and posting letters
Cleaning the sweet shop downstairs
Making tea in the morning and buying the day's supplies
e: Hari made tea in the morning and then went out to buy the day's supplies from the market, making about a rupee's profit.

q: For how long did Mr Herriot advise Mrs Pumphrey to hospitalise Tricki?
o: Two days
A week
About a fortnight (fourteen days)
Three months
e: Herriot told Mrs Pumphrey that Tricki must be hospitalised for about a fortnight to be kept under observation.

q: How much money did Hari Singh steal from under Anil's mattress?
o: 300 rupees
600 rupees in fifties
1000 rupees in hundreds
125 rupees
e: Running away, Hari counted the notes at his waist: "600 rupees in fifties!"

q: What was the name of the greyhound at Mr Herriot's surgery?
o: Sherry
Joe
Max
Guess
e: When Tricki first tottered into the yard, Joe the greyhound and his friends sniffed around him and decided he was uninteresting.

q: Which train did Hari Singh miss deliberately out of unexplained hesitation?
o: The 10:30 Express to Lucknow
The 9:15 Delhi Mail
The Midnight Bombay Express
The 6:00 Patna Passenger
e: Hari reached the platform just as the 10:30 Express to Lucknow was moving out, yet hesitated and let it depart.

q: How much medical surgery or medicine did Mr Herriot use to cure Tricki?
o: One minor operation
Special herbal tablets
Three injections daily
No medicinal treatment of any kind
e: Herriot explicitly notes, "At the surgery, the household dogs surged round me... No medicinal treatment of any kind" was given to Tricki.

q: Why did Hari Singh decide to steal Anil's money despite liking him?
o: Hari needed money to pay his school fees
Anil beat him badly
Anil didn't pay him any salary and Hari thought Anil would waste the money on friends
Anil asked him to leave the house
e: Hari rationalized the theft by telling himself Anil didn't pay him a salary and would only waste the cash on friends.

q: What did Mrs Pumphrey give Tricki between meals to "build him up"?
o: Boiled rice and milk
Fresh apples and carrots
Malt, cod-liver oil, and a bowl of Horlicks at night
Salted biscuits and tea
e: Thinking he had malnutrition, Mrs Pumphrey fed him extra malt, cod-liver oil, and a nightly bowl of Horlicks.

q: How did Anil get the bundle of 600 rupees that he tucked under his mattress?
o: From borrowing money from a friend
From selling a book to a publisher
From selling his sweet shop
From winning a wrestling match
e: One evening Anil came home happy with a small bundle of notes, saying he had just sold a book to a publisher.

q: What three items did Mr Herriot advise Mrs Pumphrey to do for Tricki at the beginning?
o: Cut his food, keep him on a strict diet, and give him more exercise
Lock him indoors and feed cream cakes
Give warm milk, bathe daily, and rest in bed
Give Horlicks, eggs, and wine
e: Dr Herriot advised cutting Tricki's food right down, removing sweets, maintaining a strict diet, and giving plenty of exercise.

q: Who was about twenty-five years old, tall, lean, easy-going, and kind?
o: Hari Singh
James Herriot
Hodgkin
Anil
e: Hari describes Anil as "about 25—a tall, lean fellow—and he looked easy-going, kind and simple enough for my purpose."

q: What did Mrs Pumphrey exclaim as she drove away with the recovered Tricki?
o: "I must fire Hodgkin immediately!"
"Tricki still needs more Horlicks!"
"Never feed dogs eggs again!"
"Oh, Mr Herriot, this is a triumph of surgery!"
e: With tears shining in her eyes, Mrs Pumphrey leaned out and cried, "Oh, Mr Herriot, how can I ever thank you? This is a triumph of surgery!"

q: What did Anil give Hari Singh the morning after Hari quietly returned the wet notes?
o: A warning letter to leave
A bus ticket to Lucknow
A fifty-rupee note and a promise of regular pay
Six hundred rupees to keep
e: Anil handed Hari a still-damp fifty-rupee note, promised to pay him regularly, and said they would start writing sentences that day.

q: Why had Tricki missed his regular ring-throwing exercise before falling seriously ill?
o: He lost all his rubber rings
Hodgkin, the gardener, had been down with lumbago
Mrs Pumphrey broke her leg
Mr Herriot forbade outdoor walks
e: Mrs Pumphrey told Herriot that because Hodgkin was laid up with lumbago, there had been no ring-throwing lately.

q: According to Hari Singh, what helps in making friends when approaching a potential victim?
o: A little flattery
Complete silence
Showing anger
Expensive gifts
e: When Anil remarked Hari also looked like a wrestler, Hari observed mentally, "A little flattery helps in making friends."

q: What alarming symptoms did Tricki show right before Mrs Pumphrey called Mr Herriot to take him away?
o: He ate nothing, refused even favourite dishes, had bouts of vomiting, and lay panting on a rug
He lost all his fur overnight
He chased the postman and barked nonstop
He climbed up trees and refused to come down
e: Within days, the expected call came: Tricki would eat nothing, had bouts of vomiting, spent all day panting on a rug, and refused walks.

q: What happened to the first meal Hari Singh cooked for Anil?
o: Anil praised it warmly
They sold it at the sweet shop
Hari threw it out of the window
It was so terrible that Anil gave it to a stray dog
e: Hari admitted he lied about knowing how to cook; the meal was so dreadful that Anil gave it to a stray dog and told Hari to leave.

q: Why did Mrs Pumphrey nearly swoon when Mr Herriot suggested hospitalising Tricki?
o: She disliked Mr Herriot's car
She wanted to take Tricki to London instead
She was sure Tricki would pine and die if he did not see her every single day
She feared the clinic fees were too high
e: Mrs Pumphrey was overly attached and convinced that Tricki could not survive a single day away from her sight.

q: Besides teaching him how to cook, what skills did Anil promise to teach Hari Singh?
o: Driving a motorcar
Writing his name, whole sentences, and adding numbers
Wrestling and swimming
Repairing locks and safes
e: Anil taught Hari to write his name and promised he would soon teach him to write whole sentences and add numbers.

q: Which items did Mrs Pumphrey's staff pack into Mr Herriot's car when Tricki left?
o: Medical bandages and dog biscuits
Day bed, night bed, cushions, toys, rubber rings, breakfast/lunch/supper bowls, and little coats
Bags of Horlicks and bottles of brandy
Gardening tools and blankets
e: Maids rushed in and out loading Tricki's day bed, night bed, cushions, toys, rubber rings, three separate meal bowls, and an armful of little coats.

q: How did Anil earn his livelihood according to Hari Singh?
o: In irregular "fits and starts"—borrowing one week and lending the next
Selling sweets at Jumna Sweet Shop
Wrestling professionally in fairs
Fixed monthly salary from a bank
e: Hari explains Anil made money "by fits and starts"—worrying about his next cheque, then celebrating as soon as one arrived.

q: Why did the other household dogs at the surgery ignore Tricki on his first day out in the garden?
o: Because he was wearing a fancy red coat
Because he barked fiercely at them
Because Mr Herriot tied him up alone
After sniffing around him, they decided the motionless fat dog was an uninteresting object
e: Joe the greyhound and his friends rolled Tricki over, sniffed him thoroughly, judged him uninteresting, and walked away.

q: How much extra profit did Hari Singh make daily while buying groceries for Anil?
o: About ten paise a day
Ten rupees a day
About a rupee a day
Fifty rupees a week
e: Hari says he usually made a profit of about a rupee a day from the shopping, and Anil knew it yet didn't seem to mind.

q: What physical activities helped transform Tricki into a "lithe, hard-muscled animal" at the surgery?
o: Massage therapy and afternoon naps
Playing catch with Mrs Pumphrey's gardener
Running with the pack, friendly scrimmages, fighting at mealtimes, and hunting rats in the old henhouse at night
Treadmill training and swimming
e: Tricki joined the dogs' pack life—scrimmages, bowl competitions, and rat-hunting at night—transforming completely within two weeks.

q: Where did Hari Singh hide the stolen 600 rupees while running away from Anil's room?
o: Inside his shirt collar
At his waist, held there by the string of his pyjamas
Inside his left shoe
Wrapped inside a newspaper under his arm
e: Hari notes, "I had the notes at my waist, held there by the string of my pyjamas."

q: In what sequence did Mrs Pumphrey send luxury delicacies to Mr Herriot's clinic for Tricki?
o: Fresh eggs first, then bottles of wine, and finally brandy
Brandy first, then chocolates, then wine
Horlicks first, then cakes, then eggs
Fish first, then wine, then biscuits
e: First came two dozen fresh eggs at a time, then bottles of wine "to enrich Tricki's blood", and finally brandy "to put a final edge on Tricki's constitution."

q: How did Hari Singh plan to spend the stolen 600 rupees once he escaped?
o: Buy a house near the station
Pay for a college degree
Open his own sweet shop
Live like an oil-rich Arab for a week or two
e: Counting the notes, Hari thought happily: "I could live like an oil-rich Arab for a week or two!"

q: Why was it a "temptation to keep Tricki on as a permanent guest" at Mr Herriot's surgery?
o: The other dogs refused to let Tricki leave
Tricki hunted all the rats in the clinic
Mrs Pumphrey forgot to call for two months
Herriot and his partners were enjoying the fresh eggs, wine, and brandy sent by Mrs Pumphrey
e: Every morning eggs, midday wine, and evening brandy made the surgery staff enjoy luxurious days courtesy of Mrs Pumphrey's parcels.

q: Why did Hari Singh avoid staying at any of the small hotels near the railway station after missing the train?
o: All hotels were closed for Diwali
He had lost all the 600 rupees on the platform
He did not want to make anyone curious by appearing alone at night with no luggage
Hotels refused guests under age eighteen
e: Having no friends and wanting not to arouse curiosity at a small hotel near the station, Hari wandered into the bazaar.

q: Which single word spoken by Mr Herriot prompted Mrs Pumphrey to start sending eggs, wine, and brandy?
o: "Infected"
"Convalescing"
"Swooning"
"Starving"
e: Herriot casually told Mrs Pumphrey Tricki was out of danger and "convalescing rapidly"—a word that triggered her flood of rich parcels.

q: What was the weather and season when Hari Singh sat on the bench in the maidan?
o: Chilly early November night with a light drizzle turning into heavy rain
Humid July monsoon morning
Hot May afternoon with dust storms
Freezing January snowfall
e: Hari describes it as "a chilly night—it was early November—and a light drizzle added to my discomfort. Soon it was raining quite heavily."

q: How did Tricki react the moment he saw Mrs Pumphrey in the reception room after two weeks?
o: He took off in a tremendous leap, sailed into her lap, swarmed over her, licked her face, and barked
He hid behind Mr Herriot's legs
He growled softly and ignored her
He walked slowly toward his day bed
e: Seeing his mistress, Tricki sprang from Herriot's arms in a huge leap, sailed into her lap, and excitedly licked her face while barking.

q: Where did Hari Singh take shelter from the heavy rain, and what time did the clock show?
o: Inside Jumna Sweet Shop at 11 p.m.
Inside an empty train coach at 1 a.m.
Under a banyan tree at 2 a.m.
Under the shelter of the clock tower at midnight
e: Soaked by the cold rain, Hari walked back to the bazaar and sat under the shelter of the clock tower, which showed midnight.

q: Why was Mrs Pumphrey's car described as "about thirty feet of gleaming black metal"?
o: To warn about traffic in London
To show it was an old broken truck
To emphasize Mrs Pumphrey's immense aristocratic wealth and chauffeur-driven luxury
To indicate Mr Herriot bought a new ambulance
e: The gleaming black chauffeur-driven limousine visually reinforces Mrs Pumphrey's extravagant wealth.

q: According to Hari Singh's careful observation, how does a "poor man" react when robbed?
o: Fear
Acceptance
Anger
Touch of sadness
e: Hari observes that the greedy man shows fear, the rich man shows anger, the poor man shows acceptance—but Anil would show sadness for the loss of trust.

q: What did Mr Herriot notice about all the beds, cushions, bowls, and coats when packing them back into the chauffeur's car?
o: They had been chewed to pieces by Joe
None of them had been used during Tricki's stay
Mrs Pumphrey asked to donate them
Tricki refused to leave without his red coat
e: Herriot remarks wryly that he helped the chauffeur bring out the beds, toys, cushions, coats, and bowls, "none of which had been used."

q: What realization under the clock tower made Hari Singh decide to return the 600 rupees to Anil?
o: He disliked walking around the bazaar forever
He realized whole sentences could bring him far more than a few hundred rupees and make him a big, respected man
He feared the police had already arrived at the station
The notes were torn beyond use
e: Sitting wet and cold, Hari understood that education ("whole sentences") would bring him far more than stolen cash and make him respected.

q: What did Mr Herriot finally say to Mrs Pumphrey on the telephone after two weeks?
o: That Tricki had recovered and was awaiting collection
That Tricki needed another month of brandy
That Tricki preferred living with Joe the greyhound
That Mrs Pumphrey should send three dozen eggs
e: Though tempted by the luxurious parcels, Herriot knew Mrs Pumphrey was suffering and felt compelled to phone her after a fortnight to collect Tricki.

q: Why does Hari Singh note that "it is much easier to steal something than to return it undetected"?
o: Because the lock on the door was jammed
Because stray dogs were barking outside
Because Anil had installed a burglar alarm
Because slipping wet notes under the mattress of a sleeping man without waking him requires extreme nerve and care
e: Stealing happened when Hari was bold and driven by greed; returning damp notes to a sleeping benefactor made him very nervous.

q: What happened on the third day at the surgery that showed Tricki was beginning to recover?
o: He slept continuously for twenty hours
He drank an entire bottle of wine alone
He began to whimper at the sound of dogs in the yard and trotted out to lick empty bowls
He barked angrily at the chauffeur
e: On the third day, Tricki whimpered when he heard dogs in the yard, trotted out, and licked inside the shining empty bowls.

q: How did Hari Singh smile at Anil at the very end of "The Thief's Story"?
o: With a forced, guilty smirk
He hid his face and cried loudly
His "most appealing" smile came by itself, without any effort
He winked cunningly at Anil
e: Whereas earlier his "most appealing smile" was practiced to manipulate Anil, at the end it arose effortlessly from genuine gratitude.

q: Why was there "no extra bowl" for Tricki on his third day until the next day?
o: Mr Herriot fed him from a silver spoon
He was jostled out during the headlong rush, licked the empty bowls later, and next day an extra bowl was put out for him
He ate only chocolates in his cage
He refused to eat with the pack
e: Once Tricki showed genuine appetite by licking empty bowls after losing the scramble, Herriot put out an extra bowl for him the next day.

q: What clue told Hari Singh on the final morning that Anil knew about the night's theft?
o: The fifty-rupee note Anil handed him was still wet from the night's rain
Anil locked the mattress in a trunk
Anil called a police constable to the room
Anil showed him muddy footprints on the floor
e: When Hari took the fifty-rupee note, he saw it was still wet from the night's rain—proving Anil knew everything yet silently forgave him.

q: Read the extract: "If you don't cut his food right down and give him more exercise he is going to be really ill. You must harden your heart..." What does "harden your heart" advise Mrs Pumphrey to do?
o: Ignore Tricki when he falls sick
Send Tricki away to another city permanently
Stop feeding him water altogether
Be firm and resist Tricki's pleading for sweet treats out of genuine concern for his health
e: Herriot warns that false tenderness—giving in to Tricki's greed for sweets—is harming him, so she must show disciplined firmness.

q: Read the extract: "It's easy to rob a greedy man, because he can afford to be robbed; but it's difficult to rob a careless man..." Why does Hari say a careless man is hard to rob?
o: Careless men always keep fierce guard dogs
Careless men carry guns under their pillows
Careless men never keep money indoors
A careless, trusting person might not even notice he's been robbed, taking all the thrill and satisfaction out of the theft
e: Hari reflects psychologically that stealing loses its sport when the victim is completely trusting and unguarded like Anil.

q: What does the word "convalescing" mean in the context of Mr Herriot's phone updates to Mrs Pumphrey?
o: Sleeping deeply under anaesthesia
Suffering a sudden relapse
Recovering health and strength gradually after an illness
Undergoing major surgery
e: "Convalescing" means regaining health after illness; Mrs Pumphrey takes this formal medical word as an excuse to send eggs, wine, and brandy.

q: In "He knew. But neither his lips nor his eyes showed anything", why did Anil hide his knowledge of the theft?
o: He planned to call the police later that afternoon
Out of deep kindness and empathy, he wanted to forgive Hari quietly and encourage his reform without shaming him
He had forgotten how much money was under his mattress
He feared Hari would run away with his books
e: By silently offering a wet 50-rupee note and promising sentence-writing lessons, Anil protected Hari's dignity and sealed his moral transformation.

q: In Mr Herriot's description of Tricki—"his eyes, bloodshot and rheumy, stared straight ahead"—what does "rheumy" mean?
o: Watery and oozing mucus due to poor health
Bright blue in colour
Tightly shut in sleep
Sparkling and alert
e: "Rheumy" refers to watery discharge from the eyes or nose caused by illness or sluggishness.

q: What does Hari Singh mean when he notices Anil's face was "clear and unlined" while his own face had "many marks, though mine were mostly scars"?
o: A sharp contrast between Anil's peaceful, honest life and Hari's harsh, dangerous past as a street thief
Anil was much younger than Hari
Anil used expensive skin creams
Hari had recently met a road accident
e: Anil's unlined face mirrors a clear conscience, whereas Hari's scars testify to a bruised, turbulent life of theft and survival.

q: Why does Mr Herriot feel "compelled to phone" Mrs Pumphrey to take Tricki home despite enjoying the eggs, wine, and brandy?
o: The wine bottles had gone sour
Joe attacked Tricki in the garden
Mrs Pumphrey threatened to sue the clinic
His professional integrity and empathy for Mrs Pumphrey's genuine anxiety outweighed selfish indulgence
e: Though amused by the temporary luxury, Herriot is a conscientious doctor who will not deceive a worried owner once her pet has fully recovered.

q: Why did Hari Singh hesitate and miss the 10:30 Express to Lucknow when he could easily have jumped aboard?
o: The ticket collector blocked the carriage door
His leg had gone numb from running
His growing conscience, attachment to Anil, and desire for education subconsciously held him back from returning to a lonely criminal life
He realized he had forgotten his shoes in Anil's room
e: Though Hari could not consciously name his hesitation at the platform, his moral bond with Anil and longing for respect kept him from fleeing.

q: What does "friendly scrimmages" mean in the line "joining in their friendly scrimmages" at the surgery?
o: Formal obedience drills
Playful rough-and-tumble tussles among the dogs
Loud midnight howling
Quiet medical check-ups
e: "Scrimmages" means lively, confused struggles or playful tussles, showing how Tricki shed his pampered laziness for healthy play.

q: Why did Hari Singh say "friends were more trouble than help"?
o: Because his school friends used to copy his homework
Because thieves live cautiously and trust no one, fearing friends might betray them or draw attention
Because Anil refused to let visitors into his room
Because he had lost a bet with a friend in Lucknow
e: As a young criminal on the run, Hari avoided close ties until Anil's unconditional trust changed his outlook completely.

q: What does Mrs Pumphrey's reaction to seeing the maid and chauffeur load unused items reveal about her?
o: She was too blinded by aristocratic habit and joy at Tricki's health to realize luxury hadn't cured him
She noticed immediately that Tricki had caught rats
She demanded a refund for the wine
She became furious with Mr Herriot for wasting money
e: Mrs Pumphrey never guesses that Tricki thrived precisely because all those cushions, coats, and luxuries were left untouched.

q: Why does Hari Singh reflect on "a touch of sadness" on Anil's face when discovering the theft?
o: Anil hated losing books to publishers
Anil would miss the delicious tea Hari made
Anil would not be able to pay his rent to the sweet shop owner
Anil would grieve not for the lost rupees, but for the betrayal of the trust he placed in Hari
e: Hari realizes Anil's reaction would be quiet sorrow over broken human trust—which pierces Hari's conscience far deeper than anger could.

q: In "stretched out in great bounds, his chest almost brushing the ground", what transformation has Tricki undergone?
o: He became timid and fearful of other dogs
He grew much shorter legs during surgery
From a breathless, bloated sausage, he became an agile, muscular, energetic dog
He became addicted to chasing cars
e: Herriot contrasts the initial bloated, wheezing Tricki with this sleek, athletic image of restored canine vitality.

q: Why did Hari Singh keep smiling in his "most appealing way" even after Anil told him to be off on the first night?
o: He saw money lying under the mattress already
He was laughing at the stray dog
He knew charm and persistence could soften an easy-going man like Anil
He wanted to mock Anil's cooking skills
e: As a street-smart teenager, Hari used practiced charm as a tool—and indeed Anil couldn't help laughing and patted him on the head.

q: What is revealed about Mrs Pumphrey's maids "rushing in and out" while loading Tricki's luggage?
o: Mr Herriot had asked for twelve beds for his clinic
Her household treated a tiny dog with absurd royal extravagance and misplaced panic
She was moving permanently to another house
Her maids hated taking care of dogs
e: An entire household staff mobilizes just to pack a dog's separate beds, cushions, and three meal bowls for a two-week stay.

q: What does "by fits and starts" mean in "He made money by fits and starts"?
o: Irregularly and unpredictably, with bursts of income followed by lean gaps
Through steady monthly paychecks
Only during wrestling tournaments
By stealing from publishers
e: "By fits and starts" is an idiom meaning in irregular bursts rather than steadily, describing Anil's freelance magazine income.

q: Why does Mr Herriot stop his car immediately when he first spots Mrs Pumphrey and Tricki walking on the street?
o: His car had run out of fuel
Hodgkin waved at him to stop
He wanted to sell her dog food
He was genuinely shocked by how dangerously swollen and unwell Tricki looked
e: As a caring veterinarian, Herriot's professional eye catches Tricki's critical obesity and red, watery eyes right away.

q: Why did Hari Singh find it easy to cheat Anil of a rupee a day yet pause at stealing the 600 rupees?
o: Because the notes were torn
Because 600 rupees was too heavy to carry in his pocket
Because Anil checked the grocery bills every night
Small petty skimming felt routine, whereas stealing Anil's entire book earnings broke Anil's total trust and ruined Hari's chance at education
e: Anil tolerated minor daily skimming out of generosity, but taking the 600 rupees forced Hari to weigh quick cash against respect and learning.

q: What does Mrs Pumphrey mean by crying, "He is listless, Mr Herriot. He seemed to have no energy"?
o: Extremely aggressive toward guests
Unable to sleep at night
Lacking energy, sluggish, and spiritless
Always hungry for meat
e: "Listless" means devoid of energy or enthusiasm—caused in Tricki's case by overeating, not malnutrition as Mrs Pumphrey assumed.

q: How does the moonlight detail ("A beam of moonlight stepped over the balcony and fell on the bed") enhance the robbery scene in "The Thief's Story"?
o: It helps Hari read Anil's book manuscript
It spotlights Anil's peaceful, trusting sleep in silence, heightening Hari's tension and guilt
It reflects off a silver knife
It wakes up the neighbours below
e: The quiet moonlight illuminating Anil's peaceful, unlined sleeping face creates cinematic stillness and sharp moral tension.

q: Why did Mrs Pumphrey phone Mr Herriot "a dozen times a day for the latest bulletins"?
o: Her anxious, doting devotion made her treat Tricki's diet rest like a critical human hospital case
She forgot Mr Herriot's clinic address

o: It makes the narrator warmly human and relatable rather than a preachy moral saint, adding self-deprecating humour
It proves veterinary doctors routinely steal from clients
It shows Herriot could not afford breakfast
It forces Mrs Pumphrey to call the police
e: Herriot's humorous honesty about enjoying the luxury parcels before doing the right thing adds charm and realism to his storytelling.

q: What crucial lesson did Hari Singh learn about the difference between stealing cash and gaining education?
o: Money stolen lasts briefly like an "oil-rich Arab for a week," whereas literacy and respect offer limitless lifelong achievement
Publishers pay less than sweet shops
Writing sentences is useful only for writing train tickets
Educated men can steal larger sums safely
e: Earlier Hari recalled: "once I could write like an educated man there would be no limit to what I could achieve"—this vision rescues him in the rain.

q: Suppose Mrs Pumphrey had stayed at the surgery every day during Tricki's recovery. What would most likely have happened?
o: Mr Herriot would have actually performed surgery
Tricki would have recovered twice as fast
Joe the greyhound would have started eating cream cakes
She would have interfered with his fasting, snuck him treats and coats, and prevented the pack exercise that cured him
e: Separating Tricki from his over-indulgent owner for a fortnight was the essential condition for resetting his diet and habits.

q: Why does Ruskin Bond set Hari's moment of inner turning in cold November rain under a clock tower showing midnight?
o: Clock towers were common shelters for stray dogs
Because November is the busiest month for book publishers
The chill, isolation, and midnight hour mirror his bleak criminal path, sharpening his contrast with the warmth and hope of Anil's room
To show Hari wanted to steal the tower clock
e: Physical discomfort in the lonely storm strips away Hari's "oil-rich Arab" fantasy, forcing honest reflection at the stroke of midnight.

q: In "A Triumph of Surgery", why doesn't Mr Herriot correct Mrs Pumphrey when she calls his simple care "a triumph of surgery"?
o: Her car drove away too quickly for him to hear
He wants to preserve her joy and let her depart happy with her healthy dog rather than embarrass her
He forgot he hadn't operated on Tricki
He secretly billed her for three operations
e: Herriot's tactful silence fits his warm, humorous temperament—Tricki is healthy, Mrs Pumphrey is ecstatic, and lecturing her would spoil the moment.

q: How would the ending of "The Thief's Story" have changed if Anil had confronted Hari angrily and handed him to the police?
o: The publisher would have taken back the book
Hari's distrust of society would have hardened, likely trapping him permanently in theft rather than inspiring self-respect and literacy
Anil would have become a famous detective
Hari would still have learned to write sentences in jail immediately
e: Returning to Anil already risked rejection; Anil's quiet forgiveness confirmed that human goodness exists, anchoring Hari's permanent reform.

q: What irony lies in Mrs Pumphrey throwing an armful of little coats through the moving car window as Tricki leaves?
o: She treats a small dog's brief stay like a pampered aristocrat's holiday wardrobe while unknowingly sending him to a muddy yard where none are needed
The coats were actually meant for Mr Herriot's children
Tricki had two separate coats for rain and snow in July
The car window was tightly closed
e: Her desperate toss of miniature raincoats and tweed coats highlights the comic gap between high-society coddling and healthy dog life.

q: What does Hari Singh's admission "It was almost a month since I had worked for Anil, and apart from cheating on the shopping, I had not done anything in my line of work" reveal?
o: Anil never left the room unattended for a month
Hari disliked stealing cash notes
Hari forgot how to pick locks
Anil's warmth and everyday companionship were already blunting Hari's criminal drive even before the 600-rupee temptation
e: Living cleanly, cooking, learning letters, and enjoying routine had quietly begun changing Hari before the final test arrived.

q: Why does Tricki's acceptance by the other dogs ("accepted him as an unlikely, silky little object among the shaggy crew") matter to his healing?
o: The dogs kept Tricki warm because he lost his coats
The shaggy dogs gave Tricki extra chocolates
Being treated as an equal pack member rather than a fragile baby forced Tricki to move, compete, and recover natural canine instincts
Tricki became leader of the pack on day one
e: Social integration among normal, active dogs cured both Tricki's physical lethargy and the behavioural spoiling caused by human over-coddling.

q: Competency: Which real-world message links both "A Triumph of Surgery" and "The Thief's Story" together in Chapter 10?
o: Wealthy people always get deceived by their helpers
Doctors and writers earn money irregularly
True care—whether for a pet or a misguided youth—relies on wisdom, discipline, and trust rather than blind indulgence or harshness
Animals understand human honesty better than humans
e: Herriot uses disciplined care to heal Tricki's body, while Anil uses wise trust and education to heal Hari's character.

q: In "The Thief's Story", why does Hari Singh call Anil "the most trusting person I had ever met" as a reason it was DIFFICULT to rob him?
o: Trusting people never keep money at home
Betraying pure, unguarded faith triggers inner guilt and removes the thief's mental justification of outsmarting a cunning rival
Hari respected writers more than wrestlers
Anil hid his keys inside the Jumna Sweet Shop
e: Stealing feels thrilling against suspicious or greedy targets, whereas robbing helpless innocence turns the thief against himself.

q: What does Tricki's night-time rat-hunting in the old henhouse signify in contrast to his earlier life on velvet cushions?
o: Complete restoration of natural instinct, courage, and physical agility freed from artificial luxury
Mrs Pumphrey's orders to train him as a guard dog
Extreme hunger because Herriot starved him for two weeks
Fear of Joe the greyhound
e: A lapdog who couldn't walk three steps without panting now hunts rats joyfully at night—a complete triumph of nature over pampering.

q: If Anil had left a stern note saying "I know you stole my money—never do it again" along with the 50 rupees, what delicate quality of his character would have been lost?
o: His ability to write clear English sentences
His friendship with the book publisher
His skill at watching wrestling matches
His quiet grace of allowing Hari to retain self-respect and choose honesty freely without public shame
e: Anil's silent tact lets Hari reform out of dignity and gratitude rather than humiliation.

q: What is comical about the contrast between Mrs Pumphrey's trembling question—"Do tell me the truth. Is he really better?"—and Tricki's immediate behaviour?
o: Tricki hides inside the limousine boot
Mr Herriot says Tricki needs three more weeks of wine
Tricki falls fast asleep on the floor
Even before Herriot answers, the energetic Tricki leaps like an acrobat into her lap and overwhelms her with joyful licks
e: Tricki himself delivers an unmistakable, boisterous answer before Herriot even finishes explaining.

q: Why does Hari Singh mention twice in "The Thief's Story" that "it was an easy job" or "a simple matter to steal"?
o: To encourage readers to try pickpocketing
To boast that he was the best thief in Lucknow
To contrast the trivial cleverness of petty crime with the far nobler, demanding discipline of education and integrity
To complain that Anil's lock was broken
e: Framing theft as easy and unremarkable raises learning to read and earning respect into the truly heroic goal.

q: How does James Herriot use medical terms like "regimen," "convalescing," and "bulletins" to add satire to "A Triumph of Surgery"?
o: It makes the story sound like a strict medical textbook
Applying solemn hospital vocabulary to a greedy little lapdog's simple diet rest mocks human exaggeration and pampering
It shows Mrs Pumphrey wanted to become a nurse
It warns readers never to use telephones
e: Mock-heroic medical language magnifies the comedy of treating overfeeding with dramatic hospital solemnity.

q: What subtle change in Hari Singh's mindset explains why he didn't even try stealing Anil's money again on the final morning?
o: His values shifted from quick survival scams to long-term self-respect, literacy, and gratitude toward Anil
Hari broke his wrist during the rainstorm
The sweet shop owner promised Hari a job
Anil hid the remaining 550 rupees inside his shoe
e: Even before Anil hands him the wet fifty-rupee note, Hari had internally chosen an honest future over stolen cash.

q: Why was Mrs Pumphrey's "mistaken diagnosis" (malnutrition) actually dangerous for Tricki?
o: It made her cure lethargy caused by overeating with EVEN MORE rich food (malt, cod-liver oil, Horlicks), creating a vicious cycle
It kept Hodgkin away from gardening
Malnutrition requires surgical removal of ears
Cod-liver oil turns dogs blind immediately
e: Treating the symptom (listlessness) by multiplying its actual cause (excess calories) pushed Tricki close to fatal collapse.

q: Competency: Why is Ruskin Bond's choice of a fifteen-year-old first-person narrator ("I") essential to the impact of "The Thief's Story"?
o: Fifteen-year-olds cannot speak in third person
Because Anil did not know how to speak English
Because Ruskin Bond wanted to describe wrestling rules
Witnessing his cynical street logic gradually soften into guilt, fear, and longing for respect lets readers experience moral awakening from within
e: First-person narration invites readers inside Hari's inner struggle between habit and conscience.

q: Which detail from "A Triumph of Surgery" shows that Tricki's recovery brought joy not just to Tricki, but also improved Mr Herriot's professional satisfaction?
o: Charging double fees for the unused bowls
Keeping Joe and Tricki together permanently
Watching the once helpless lump sprint effortlessly in great bounds with the pack and watching his joyful reunion with Mrs Pumphrey
Receiving a gold medal from the city mayor
e: Despite humorous envy over losing the eggs and brandy, Herriot takes genuine pride in restoring Tricki through pure common sense and nature.

q: Evaluate why "The Thief's Story" never reveals the young thief's real birth name even at the end.
o: Because thieves in India have no names
Because his past identity didn't matter as much as the new, honest identity he is about to build under Anil's mentorship as Hari Singh
Because Ruskin Bond forgot to write his real name
Because he was actually Anil's younger brother
e: Leaving his birth name untold keeps focus on his universal vulnerability and his choice to become someone worthy of respect.
